title: ask-constellation-mini-scan-nov-2025
content:
Purpose: quick synth of recent customer asks (Nov intake window) using a ‘constellation’ metaphor — map discrete asks as stars, cluster into constellations to reveal cross-customer patterns. Meant for fast triage and low-effort pilot proposals.

Scope and data sources:
- Inputs: 28 inbound CS tickets (JIRA), five recorded customer calls (notes), three support chat transcripts, product telemetry spikes (embedding latency and error rates), two partner field reports.
- Time window: 2025-10-25 -> 2025-11-05.
- Quick note: this is deliberately minimal — not exhaustive; purpose is to surface candidate micro-features and operational patches.

Topline (executive TL;DR):
- Recurring theme: stability-of-inference under bursty traffic and model-fallback behavior causing inconsistent latencies and user-visible tail errors. Appears across SMB PLG customers and one enterprise (regulated) customer.
- High-opportunity low-effort asks: (1) clearer client-side retry hints / recommended retry strategies in SDK, (2) a lightweight “fallback transparency” flag that returns which model variant served the request, (3) a small console toggle to opt into prefix caching for chat sessions.
- Risky / larger asks: dedicated routing contracts, SLA upgrades, private deployment changes. Flagging for product/eng roadmap.

Constellation mapping (stars -> clusters):
- Star: "burst-latency-spikes" (reported by 9 customers). Symptoms: 95/99th latency spikes, partial tokens dropped in stream. Telemetry: p99 token latency +80% during 10–30s bursts. Representative quote: "Responses freeze about 10–20s, then stream catches up with garbled text."
- Star: "model-variant-opaque-fallbacks" (6 customers). Symptoms: customers see different output quality when routed to quantized/low-cost variants; no metadata returned to caller. Quote: "We had to guess why tone changed mid-conversation."
- Star: "embedding-drift-notice" (4 customers, embedding similarity degradation over long tails). Symptoms: older cached embeddings not invalidated; customers reindex manually.
- Star: "console-batching-visibility" (5 customers). Need per-route batching metrics, suggested by platform teams.
- Cluster: "operational hygiene" groups burst-latency-spikes + console-batching-visibility + model-variant-opaque-fallbacks -> suggests product/ops surfaces for observability and SDK hints.

Prioritization grid (quick heuristic):
- Quick wins (impact >= medium, effort = low):
  1) SDK retry guidance + code snippet in docs (owner: devexp) — Impact: medium, Effort: low. Tickets: JIRA-CS-1421.
  2) Response metadata flag: return model_variant_id + quantization_profile (owner: serving-runtime) — Impact: high for debugging, Effort: low-medium. Quick patch: include header or first-chunk event.
  3) Console toggle: prefix cache opt-in per-model route (owner: product-hosted-api) — Impact: medium, Effort: low.

- Medium projects (impact = high, effort = medium):
  1) Per-route batching & token-cost telemetry (dashboards + API) — owner: observability. Requires schema additions to ingestion pipeline.
  2) Guided fallback policy builder (UI + policy DSL) — owner: product/rollouts. Enables predictable degradation.

- Investment bets (impact = high, effort = high):
  1) SLA-tier routing + reserved warm pools for enterprise bursts (owner: dedicated). Longer lead time.

Customer vignettes (short):
- SMB analytics tool (startup): experienced p99 stutters when users import large files during onboarding spike; implemented client-side exponential backoff; still hit quality variance when fallback to q4-8-bit models. Wants a simple header that says which variant was used.
- Regulated fintech (large): wants deterministic rollouts — ability to pin model families per route and to audit fallback events (who/when/why). Also asked for KMS audit samples.
- Platform team inside mid-market customer: asked for per-route batching insights to show cost-savings to their internal stakeholders.

Suggested low-risk patches (actionable, <2 weeks engineer effort each):
1) Docs + SDK snippet: Recommended retry/backoff, sample pseudocode for streaming resumes. (Owner: devexp)
2) Add a single boolean response field: "x_model_variant_hint" (Owner: serving-runtime) — default off, customer opt-in via header. Minimal contract change; surfaces cause of quality shift.
3) Console checkbox: Enable prefix caching for route X (owner: product). Backend maps to existing cache flag; UI only.
4) Short-term telemetry: emit an event when fallback occurs with route, timestamp, variant_id (owner: observability) — retention short-term for debugging.

Operational notes and caveats:
- Adding variant metadata increases surface area for security/PII review — ensure no customer data leaks, include in compliance review.
- Telemetry volume could spike — add sampling (1%) for initial rollout.
- UI toggle must be gated by role (admin) and org-level setting for private deployments.

Open questions (for sync with eng/product):
- For variant metadata, do we return full model name or just opaque id? (tradeoff: debugability vs leak of internal naming).
- Is a console prefix-caching toggle supported by existing runtime flags or does it need a migration?
- Can observability emit fallback events without schema churn?

Proposed next steps (owners & timelines):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize list and get engineering quick-OKs on variant_hint field (owner: Aisha / serving-runtime).
- Week 1: docs + SDK retry snippet PR (owner: devexp / Tomás).
- Week 2: deploy variant_hint default-off flag behind experiment and enable sampling for fallback events (owner: observability / Maya).
- Week 3–4: console checkbox UX mock + small backend mapping (owner: product-hosted-api / Evan).

Slack & follow-ups: see linked artifacts for the raw transcripts and the JIRA cluster. Scheduling: propose 30-minute triage w/serving-runtime, observability, and devexp on 2025-11-14.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Could prototype variant_hint as part of the first-chunk stream event (less schema churn).
- Consider an "explainable-fallback" doc for customers explaining cost vs quality tradeoffs and routing policies — helps CS conversations.

Appendix: raw sample quotes (redacted)
- "When the model switched mid-chat we lost our tone continuity — hard to debug." — SMB analytics tool
- "We need to know when an inference degraded and why; auditing fallbacks is a must for us." — fintech
- "Dashboard doesn't tell us if batching saved us money per-route." — internal platform team

End of mini-scan. This is intentionally pragmatic — recommend shipping 2–3 low-risk patches to improve immediate visibility and provide relief to multiple customers.
